newsitem.title: FRANCE: S. Korea's Daewoo establishes fourth French plant.
newsitem.headline: S. Korea's Daewoo establishes fourth French plant.

text.p: South Korea's Daewoo Electronics, still keen on France despite a public rejection of its bid for state-owned Thomson Multimedia, said on Wednesday it was setting up a fourth plant in eastern France.

Chairman Soon-Hoon Bae said the group would invest 1.74 billion francs ($302.1 million) to set up a plant making television and computer screens in the town of Thionville, creating 700 jobs in the next three years, the French industry ministry said.

"Daewoo thus confirms the industrial strategy of its presence in France which represent 1,200 jobs. Thanks to this project and the expansion of its French plants announced in 1996, Daewoo will employ 2,700 people in France in the coming years," the ministry said in a statement.

Daewoo was waiting for new terms to be set for the privatisation of French consumer electronics company Thomson Multimedia (TMM), before making any fresh bid and indicated that there were certain parameters to be met, Soon-Hoon Bae told reporters.
"I have to see the new procedure before I say I am interested or not," he said.

Last year Daewoo teamed up with Lagardere in a failed bid for the state-owned Thomson SA electronics firm. Lagardere had agreed to sell money-losing TMM to Daewoo and keep Thomson's defence electronics unit, Thomson-CSF .
The deal was initially approved by the French government but scrapped after the independent Privatisation Commission objected.
The Daewoo chairman said he had felt "bitter" over the decision of the commission, which he said gave Daewoo's foreign status as its main reason for objection.
He thought it was strange that the French state rejected a foreign bid for a company but was ready to accept inward investment.

The French government is contributing a quarter of the total investment in the new Daewoo factory, representing the maximum allowed by the European Commission. The regional aid comes to more than 400 million francs, a French official said.

Asked if Daewoo would accept a minority stake in TMM rather than buying the whole company, he said, "I cannot say yes or no. Up to now we have been thinking about buying the whole of Thomson Multimedia. We have not thought about a sale in parts."
The government's decision to cancel the sale, which also followed a public outcry tinged with xenophobia, mushroomed into a diplomatic incident between the Seoul and Paris governments.
In Rabat, a spokesman for Daewoo Corp said the group remained "extremely interested" in TMM.
TMM is due to get an 11 billion franc state recapitalisation to prepare for privatisation.
The French government on Tuesday appointed Thierry Breton, a former senior manager at recently-privatised Compagnie des Machines Bull , to head TMM and prepare its sale.
It said TMM would be sold gradually through the opening up of its capital, much the way Bull was privatised. It has already launched the privatisation of the profitable Thomson-CSF.
